shared_elements: horizontal band of small repeated motifs running across the upper part of the surface
animal imagery (bovid skull with horns in A; relief quadrupeds and birds in B)
register-like stacking of motifs above/below the band
justification: The only real correspondence is organisational: both surfaces carry a horizontal band of small repeated units across the upper zone, with larger animal-related elements set below or beside it, and both share a buff-ochre tonality. Otherwise they could hardly be more different in manner — A is flat red painted geometric marks on smooth white plaster with an actual mounted horned skull and antlers on the floor, while B is a monolithic stone slab worked in low relief with modelled birds, quadrupeds, a disc and looped arch forms, so the shared traits are generic rather than a shared compositional scheme.
